The Second Western District Military Court has sentenced Dmitry Bokov, a 19-year-old student at the Russian State University for the Humanities, to 19 years in prison for plotting a terrorist attack on a mosque. Ostorozhno, Novosti and Msk1 reported the sentence, citing his relatives.

Actual Article Body:
The Second Western District Military Court has sentenced Dmitry Bokov, a 19-year-old student at the Russian State University for the Humanities, to 19 years in prison for plotting a terrorist attack on a mosque. Ostorozhno, Novosti and Msk1 reported the sentence, citing his relatives.

Bokov was convicted of undergoing training for terrorist activities (Article 205.3 of Russia’s Criminal Code), preparing to join a terrorist organization (Article 205.5), weapons offenses (Article 222), and preparing a terrorist attack (Article 205).

The 17-year-old Franklin High School student who fell from a fourth-floor railing last week on campus died by suicide, according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office.

In an online database, the Los Angeles County medical examiner listed the manner of death for Xavier Nungaray-Martinez on Tuesday and noted he suffered from multiple blunt traumatic injuries to the head and torso.

Officials have not released details about what preceded the fall.

NEW YORK — Student loan borrowers now have until the end of 2026 to enroll in auto pay and have their interest rate reduced by 1%.

The original deadline was Sept. 30, but the U.S. Department of Education extended it to give borrowers more time to enroll. The rate reduction will last through June 2028.

Borrowers who currently use auto pay already receive an interest-rate discount of 0.25%, so the new reduction takes off just 0.75%.

This temporary benefit is meant to support borrowers, along with those who are returning to repayment, and ensure they can stay on top of the new Repayment Assistance Plan that requires on-time payments, according to the Education Department.
